key_insight: The paper makes operator learning self-explainable by decomposing predictions into localized integral contributions, revealing which spatial regions drive outputs.
engineering_relevance: This gives fluid-mechanics models built-in interpretability, helping engineers trust and diagnose predictions in blood flow and aerodynamics applications.
method: Reformulate operator learning as a linear combination of generalized functional linear models via integral equations.
Partition the input domain into subdomains and compute localized integrals to measure regional influence.
Link input regions to output patterns directly, producing intrinsic explanations for function-to-scalar and function-to-function mappings.
evidence_signal: The framework was tested on blood flow and unsteady aerodynamics problems, where it consistently highlighted high-gradient regions and showed qualitative agreement with post-hoc explainability methods.
watch_item: The approach relies on careful subdomain partitioning and integral evaluation, which may affect interpretability and accuracy if the spatial discretization is poorly chosen.
paper_title: Self-explainable Operator Learning for Discovering Spatial Patterns in Functional Data
